Hi Jordan / Alicia,

Thanks again for your time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what I heard from the demo/discovery call:
- MedSecure will be processing PHI; HIPAA coverage and a signed BAA are mandatory.
- You prefer a Private VPC/on-prem option for the highest data isolation, but are open to Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) if it reduces operational burden and meets audit requirements.
- SOC 2 Type II evidence is required for your procurement team — in particular: system description, control mapping, and sample audit logs / retention details.
- Critical questions for you: encryption/key management (customer-managed keys?), network egress/allowlist model, and log retention/format for audits.

What I am attaching: a short SOC2 summary (Redwood_SOC2_Summary.pdf) and a draft BAA (BAA_Draft_Redwood.docx) so legal can start review. These are high-level — we should follow with the exact artifacts your auditors need.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive (security + infra) to surface whether Private VPC (customer-managed infra) is required or Dedicated satisfies the controls you need. I suggest 60 minutes and we bring our infra lead (Sean) and your infra/security contact.
2) Legal/Procurement sync to review the BAA draft and any redlines (Marissa on our side will help).
3) Share specific audit artifacts you need (sample audit logs, retention SLA, diagram of key flows). If you can list top 6 items, we’ll prioritize delivering them.

Open items I will answer in a follow-up email: PKI/KMS options and log retention defaults across hosting modes.

Proposed times: Thu 9/9 10am PT or Mon 9/13 2pm PT for the tech deep-dive — what works best?

Thanks, Evelyn — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side (Alicia is our compliance lead, looping her in):

1) Deployment preference: our security review currently leans toward Private VPC or on-prem (customer-controlled network) because we need full control over key management and egress. If Redwood Dedicated can support customer-managed keys and strict egress allowlists, it would remain on the table.
2) Data residency: all data must remain in US regions.
3) Retention: we need to confirm legal retention requirements, but planning for 7 years of audit logs is likely. Can you confirm Redwood’s ability to retain immutable audit logs for 7+ years?
4) Encryption and keys: we need to know whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS/HSM in Private and Dedicated modes, and what the default is for Hosted.
5) Incident/notification SLAs: what is your standard window for security incident notification to customers?

For the tech deep-dive, Thu 9/9 10am PT works for us. Please include any runbooks showing how logs are captured/sent for audits.

Jordan / Alicia — thanks for the clarifications, and great to see Alicia on the thread. High-level answers to your questions below; we’ll cover details in the tech call.

- Deployment modes and keys:
  * Private VPC / on-prem: supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. If you run the control plane or provide your own HSM, you control keys.
  * Redwood Dedicated: supports customer-managed keys via our KMS-integration option (we can provision a customer key or integrate with your cloud KMS via a constrained role). We treat this as a contractual option and will document key rotation policies.
  * Hosted API: default uses Redwood-managed KMS (AES-256 at rest). We can discuss a hybrid approach but customer-managed keys typically require Dedicated or Private deployments.

- Audit logs & retention:
  * We capture structured request/response metadata, auth events, and deployment changes. Standard retention in Hosted is 90 days; Dedicated/Private options are configurable — we can provide an immutable export or longer retention windows (7+ years) for Dedicated/Private with an archival runbook.

- Network / egress model:
  * Private VPC: fully customer-controlled allowlists and NAT egress.
  * Dedicated: VPC peering or private link options with a controlled egress path; we can restrict outbound endpoints.

- Incident notifications:
  * Standard security incident notification: initial acknowledgement within 2 hours, full customer notification with impact summary within 48 hours for severity-1 incidents. We can discuss contractual SLA tightening for enterprise agreements.

Proposed immediate actions I will own:
- Share the SOC2 summary and editable BAA (attached previously).
- Sean will take the tech deep-dive and bring runbook examples for audit log exports and retention.
- Marissa will coordinate legal review on any BAA redlines.

Sean / Marissa — can you both confirm availability Thu 9/9 10am PT? I’ll send a calendar invite when confirmed.

Thanks,
Evelyn
